standards_cli.behavior: check --fix applies the complete configured rule set before reporting remaining findings. format/fix use the same safe-fix orchestration. Partially staged files are rejected before mutation; staged fixes remain unstaged for review. Deleted index entries are excluded from mutation targets even when an untracked worktree copy remains; deleted metadata still triggers its existing repository checks. Invalid output options are rejected before source fixes. Successful staged fixes emit review-required results in the requested text, JSON or SARIF format.

policy.behavior: Use the same selected paths, enabled capabilities and per-file rule exclusions as checking. Repository ESLint execution requires the existing trust opt-in. Ruff uses --no-unsafe-fixes. Native source APIs honor selection, suppressions and their own generated/ownership exclusions.

ruff_configuration.behavior: Checking, safe Ruff fixes and formatting reuse the same per-file project/configuration authority, including adopted fallback configurations. Selected paths and per-file excluded rule groups remain separate; safe fixes retain --no-unsafe-fixes.

generated_usage_docs.behavior: Generated package usage explains automatic staged hook fixes, review/restaging and the shared check --fix/fix --staged entry points. upstream_api_baseline.behavior: Retain upstream lazy changed-scope loading and diagnostic-baseline implementation alongside the candidate fix entry points. Current implementation/regression inputs are frozen; the native suite owns their behavioral validation.

upstream_retired_suppressions.behavior: Retain the exact upstream retirement-tokenization implementation and regression tests. Current inputs are frozen; native behavioral qualification remains pending.

formatted_code_examples.behavior: Use the canonical npm code-examples:sync output generated under supervised pinned tools, including Terraform1.15.8. The output is frozen with the candidate; full documentation/native qualification remains separate.

hooks.behavior: Managed Lefthook/pre-commit entries invoke staged check --fix with existing trust policy; remaining diagnostics still fail checking. Changed files are not automatically staged.

fixer_failures.behavior: Signal-terminated external fixers normalize to infrastructure status 2 and stop later tools. A normal status 1 can leave findings while subsequent configured fixers continue. Machine-output operations keep external tool stdout off the structured stdout stream. Encoding/header failures and failed external fixers produce a failed report in the requested machine format/destination with status2, without running later analysis or claiming findings are complete; tool failures require review of any partial changes.

source_edits.behavior: Native text edits use Unicode codepoint ranges, bounds and overlap validation; language owners separately prove parse/token/value preservation.

source_writes.behavior: Shared native writer preserves source encoding/BOM and newline bytes, preserves and verifies ordinary permission bits and group ownership, and refuses source SUID/SGID. It refuses symlinks, hardlinks, nonregular files and all detected source or temporary extended attributes, including ACLs, user notes and security/capability labels; inspection failures refuse changes. Temporary metadata is rechecked after fsync, and source bytes, identity and metadata are rechecked before atomic per-file replacement. It does not copy security metadata. On platforms without extended-attribute inspection, absence cannot be proven and unsupported metadata preservation is not claimed. A multi-file operation is not a single filesystem transaction.

example_contract.behavior: Native fixed_files examples require exact expected source, absence of the owned finding and an unchanged second fix pass.

hidden_index_guard.behavior: Before staged check/fix mutation, refuse selected assume-unchanged or skip-worktree index entries, including combined flags and clean flagged entries. NUL-delimited literal-path selection preserves exact filenames and unrelated flagged entries; failed Git reads report infrastructure failure.

rules.safe_subset_or_rejected_boundary: Autofix only adds a matching assert_awaited_once[_with] after the original call assertion in an argument-free, undecorated module async test whose exact body creates a fresh unconfigured canonical AsyncMock, awaits it once, and asserts its single call. limitations: Only direct statements in collected test functions and methods are inspected; fixtures, helpers, nested blocks, and generated files are excluded.
Requires a fresh local unittest.mock.AsyncMock constructor with unshadowed imports; aliases, reassignment, reset, and ambiguous configuration are excluded.
Visible provider replacement, escape or unresolved lexical ownership retains WARNING; only the closed canonical AsyncMock provider proof blocks.
Only the mock itself and unchanged immediate children of unspecced, unwrapped mocks are inferred; spec children, return values, and deeper chains are excluded.
Positive call evidence includes direct assertion methods and literal numeric or boolean call-state checks; unresolved call expectations are excluded.

Await evidence excludes provably vacuous checks, including non-None count/list state, zero or nonnegative numeric bounds, and empty expected await sequences; unresolved expectations are accepted without inferring their values.
Length comparisons over await_args_list use count semantics only for an unshadowed builtin len without visible builtin namespace access; custom length functions remain unresolved.
